findings.title: Three tracked root-level test files bypass the entire credential-strip conftest and call live paid vendors
findings.claim: `test_services.py`, `test_client.py` and `phase0_test.py` sit at the repo ROOT (outside `tests/`), so `tests/conftest.py`'s `neutralize_credentials()` and the live-tier skip hook never apply to them, yet pytest collects 12 test nodes from them that call live OpenAI / Serper / Upstash / Supabase / Firecrawl / Scrape.do with the developer's real `.env`.
findings.evidence: `test_services.py:10` does `load_dotenv()` at module scope and `:18` reads the real `OPENAI_API_KEY`; `phase0_test.py:10` does the same and `:34` calls `firecrawl_service.scrape_page_with_status()` against a live bloomingdales.ae URL. `git ls-files --error-unmatch` reports all three TRACKED. `pyproject.toml` [tool.pytest.ini_options] sets no `testpaths`, and `python -m pytest --collect-only -q test_services.py test_client.py phase0_test.py` collected `12 tests` (test_openai, test_serper, test_redis, test_supabase, test_quick_comparison, test_health, test_rate_limit, test_quick_compare, test_image_compare, test_history, test_firecrawl, test_scrapedo). None carries a live_unit/live_db/integration marker, so `-m "not (live_unit or live_db or integration)"` does NOT deselect them. `find . -name test_*.py -not -path ./tests/*` also finds `backend/test_client.py` and `backend/test_services.py`.
findings.failure_scenario: A developer or agent runs bare `pytest` (or `pytest -k firecrawl`, or an IDE 'run tests in workspace') from the repo root instead of the documented `pytest tests/ ...`. Collection picks up the 12 root nodes; `phase0_test.py::test_firecrawl` and `::test_scrapedo` spend real Firecrawl/Scrape.do credits against a live storefront, `test_services.py::test_openai` bills OpenAI, `test_services.py::test_redis` writes to the PRODUCTION Upstash cache, and `test_services.py::test_supabase` queries production Supabase. Every protection issue #48 built (`tests/_env_safety.py`) is bypassed because the conftest that installs it is one directory below.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `testpaths = ["tests"]` to `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` and rename the three root scripts out of the `test_*.py` collection pattern (e.g. `scripts/manual/smoke_services.py`) or move them under `scripts/`. Add a `tests/test_ci_gates.py` guard asserting `list(REPO_ROOT.glob('test_*.py')) == []` so the class cannot come back.

findings.title: The entire 135-file Jest estate is never executed: no npm test script and no CI job
findings.claim: `SmartCompareApp/__tests__/` holds 135 Jest test files with a full `jest.config.js` and the jest/ts-jest/@testing-library devDependencies installed, but `package.json`'s `scripts` block contains only `start/android/ios/web/lint` — there is no `test` script — and neither `.github/workflows/ci.yml` nor `live-suite.yml` runs jest.
findings.evidence: `SmartCompareApp/package.json:5-11` = `{start, android, ios, web, lint}` only; `:57-68` lists `@testing-library/react-native`, `@types/jest`, `jest ^29.7.0`, `ts-jest`. `SmartCompareApp/jest.config.js` is a 55-line config with testMatch, 20 moduleNameMapper shims and `setupFilesAfterEach: __tests__/setup.ts`. `ls SmartCompareApp/__tests__ | wc -l` = 135. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` frontend job (lines 189-205) runs only `npx tsc --noEmit`. CLAUDE.md:299 still cites Jest coverage numbers ("HomeScreen 35->82%, Profile 0->82%, EditProfile 0->97%") as if the suite is a live gate.
findings.failure_scenario: Any React Native change — an OnboardingFlow step reorder, a DimensionBars delta guard, an auth screen regression — merges with zero automated frontend verification. The 135 suites can only rot: nobody can even run them with a documented command, so a suite that started failing months ago is indistinguishable from one that passes, and the coverage figures in CLAUDE.md are unfalsifiable.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `"test": "jest"` and `"test:ci": "jest --ci --coverage"` to `SmartCompareApp/package.json`, then add a `frontend-tests` job to ci.yml (`npm ci && npm test`). Land it non-blocking first to measure the current red count, then flip to blocking the same way `backend-lint` was ratcheted.

findings.title: The repo's real regression gate is a local-only script; CI runs a raw pytest that is red by construction
findings.claim: `scripts/regression_gate_diff.py` (the baseline-subset "no NEW failures" gate the whole process depends on) is referenced by no workflow and no git hook, while `ci.yml`'s `backend-tests` step runs bare `pytest tests/` including the 11-15 known-failing nodes, so the job can never go green and therefore can never become a required status check.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn regression_gate_diff .github/ .githooks/` returns nothing; the only consumer is `tests/test_regression_gate_diff.py`. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:86-96` is `pytest tests/ -m "not (live_unit or live_db or integration)" --ignore=tests/test_integration.py --timeout=60 -rxX --cov=app --cov-fail-under=83` with no `--deselect` of the baseline and no `continue-on-error`. `docs/investigations/2026-08-25-audit-wave1-handoff.md:11` records `backend-tests` as still failing (15 failed / 9,653 passed) after the #86 gate landed. I re-measured the surviving baseline in isolation: 11 failed / 1 passed / 1 node-id-not-found.
findings.failure_scenario: Every PR shows `backend-tests` red. A genuine regression that adds a 16th failure is visually identical to the standing 15, so reviewers stop reading the job; `--cov-fail-under=83`, the `Lock is current` drift gate and the `Syntax check` step all sit in the same job and their signal is lost with it. ci.yml:98-103 already documents that branch protection cannot list this job until it is green — so the pipeline has four jobs and zero enforced gates on `main`.
findings.fix_sketch: Either (a) add a `known-red` deselect file consumed by `--deselect @tests/known_red.txt` so backend-tests can be green and required, or (b) replace the raw pytest step with `pytest ... || true` piped into `python -m scripts.regression_gate_diff --baseline tests/.pre_impl_failures.txt`, making `branch-only-NEW == []` the exit code. Option (b) is what the team already does by hand.

findings.title: Baselined as 'intentional': two failing tests are pinning a raw Supabase error string returned to end users
findings.claim: `tests/test_auth_interceptor.py::test_sign_in_with_social_exception` and `::test_social_login_user_insert_fails_gracefully` are listed in the baseline as "[B4-BE-DIAG] Google-sign-in diagnostic string intentionally present", but what they actually catch is a live code path that returns the raw provider exception text to the API client instead of the generic user-facing message.
findings.evidence: `app/services/auth_service.py:61-65`: `if context == "social_login": return {"success": False, "error": f"[B4-BE-DIAG] supabase_error={str(e)[:300]} exc_type={type(e).__name__}"}`. The comment at `:54-60` is dated 2026-05-26 and ends "REMOVE this branch after B4 ships green + clean." Measured this tree: both tests fail with `assert '[B4-BE-DIAG] supabase_error=Provider error exc_type=Exception' == 'Something went wrong. Please try again later.'`. `tests/PRE_IMPL_FAILURE_BASELINE.md:52` classifies them as intentional.
findings.failure_scenario: A user hits any unclassified Supabase failure during Google/Apple sign-in (rate limit, RLS denial, schema error, a message embedding an internal identifier). The first 300 characters of the raw provider exception plus the exception class name are returned in the API response body and rendered on-screen by the FE's [B4-DIAG] wrapper — three months after the diagnostic's own removal note. The two tests that would flag it were reclassified as expected failures, so the removal deadline has no enforcement.
findings.fix_sketch: Delete the `social_login` branch (auth_service.py:61-65), restoring the generic return at `:66`; the two tests go green and leave the baseline. If the diagnostic is still wanted, gate it on an env flag that is OFF in prod and add the flag-ON/flag-OFF pair to the tests instead of baselining the failure.

findings.title: Baselined as 'mock drift': the 3 camera_vision failures are an unguarded crash on the identify_products main path
findings.claim: The three `tests/test_camera_vision.py::TestIdentifyProductsMocked` failures are recorded as "mock drift, unrelated", but the traceback shows `_log_cache_telemetry` raising out of `identify_products` because the telemetry call is not wrapped in try/except — a non-numeric `cached_tokens` from any SDK/proxy shape kills the whole vision request.
findings.evidence: `app/services/openai_service.py:97` is `if cached_tokens > 0:` after a `getattr` chain that can yield a non-numeric object; `:211` calls `_log_cache_telemetry(response, "identify_products")` at statement level with no surrounding try/except (the nearest try at `:216` only wraps `json.loads`). Measured traceback: `app/services/openai_service.py:211 -> :97 TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'MagicMock' and 'int'`. Same unguarded pattern at `:300`, `:375`, `:437`. `tests/PRE_IMPL_FAILURE_BASELINE.md:50` calls it mock drift.
findings.failure_scenario: The function's own docstring says it must tolerate "older SDK drafts and some Anthropic/proxy implementations". Point `OPENAI_BASE_URL` at a proxy (a supported, already-neutralised env var) that returns `usage.prompt_tokens_details` as a dict rather than an object, or `prompt_tokens_cached` as the string "0": `getattr(details, 'cached_tokens', 0)` returns the default or a str, `cached_tokens > 0` raises TypeError, and the camera-comparison endpoint 500s instead of returning products. A telemetry log line takes down a paid feature.
findings.fix_sketch: Coerce before comparing (`try: cached_tokens = int(cached_tokens) except (TypeError, ValueError): return`) and wrap all four `_log_cache_telemetry` call sites in `try/except Exception: pass`. The three tests then go green and leave the baseline.

findings.title: The locked 48-node failure baseline is stale three different ways and its two source files disagree
findings.claim: Of the 48 baseline node ids, 35 can never be reported again (xfail-contained), one no longer exists in the tree, one now passes, and the human-readable table sums to 49 including a node the machine-readable mirror does not contain — so the number everyone quotes ("the last 15") matches neither file.
findings.evidence: (a) `tests/.pre_impl_failures.txt:24` = `tests/test_lane1_helpers_unit.py::test_compose_delta_text_returns_empty_on_missing_score_sentinel`; running it gives `ERROR: not found ... (no match in any of [<Module test_lane1_helpers_unit.py>])`. (b) `tests/.pre_impl_failures.txt:29` = `tests/test_source_usage_field.py::test_registry_price_source_count`; `pytest tests/test_source_usage_field.py` = `13 passed`. (c) `tests/PRE_IMPL_FAILURE_BASELINE.md:49-59` counts 35+3+2+2+1+1+1+1+1+1+1 = 49 and asserts at `:30` "The real-GET rate-limit test IS in the 48 baseline" — `grep test_rate_limiting_complete tests/.pre_impl_failures.txt` returns nothing. (d) `scripts/regression_gate_diff.py:38` still describes the mirror as "byte-for-set identical to QA's 59" while both files hold 48.
findings.failure_scenario: The gate is a subset check so stale entries only ever forgive, but the denominator is the thing humans act on. Someone fixing "the last 15" opens `.pre_impl_failures.txt`, works a node id that no longer exists, and concludes the tree is broken; or reads the markdown table, budgets for 49, and cannot reconcile it with 48. Worse, the now-passing `test_registry_price_source_count` is still forgiven by the gate: if a future change deletes registry rows and re-breaks it, `branch-only-NEW` stays empty and the regression merges.
findings.fix_sketch: Re-capture the baseline on a clean tree (`pytest ... -q | grep ^FAILED | sort > tests/.pre_impl_failures.txt`), delete the two dead ids, regenerate the markdown table from the file rather than by hand, and add a `test_ci_gates` assertion that every baseline node id still resolves to a collected node.

findings.title: The regression gate's default baseline is an absolute path into one developer's other checkout
findings.claim: `DEFAULT_BASELINE` resolves to `C:\Users\SynAckITPC\Documents\AI\smartcompare\.qa-discovery\BASELINE_FAILURES.txt` when that path happens to exist on the machine, and to the committed mirror otherwise — so the same command gates against different, unversioned data depending on who runs it and on the state of an unrelated working copy.
findings.evidence: `scripts/regression_gate_diff.py:42-49`: `_QA_CANONICAL_BASELINE = Path(r"C:\Users\SynAckITPC\Documents\AI\smartcompare\.qa-discovery\BASELINE_FAILURES.txt")` then `DEFAULT_BASELINE = _QA_CANONICAL_BASELINE if _QA_CANONICAL_BASELINE.exists() else _LOCAL_BASELINE_SNAPSHOT`. That path EXISTS on this machine (verified with `ls`), and `.gitignore` ignores `.qa-*/` so the file it points at can never be reviewed, diffed or restored. The two files currently agree on the id set but differ in format (QA's lines carry a `FAILED ` prefix).
findings.failure_scenario: Ahmed edits or regenerates `.qa-discovery/BASELINE_FAILURES.txt` in the sibling `smartcompare` checkout — adding an id to unblock a branch. Every subsequent gate run on this machine silently forgives that id while CI, a fresh clone, and every other agent read the committed 48-id mirror and would still call it a regression. Two people run "the same gate" and get opposite verdicts, with nothing in git recording why.
findings.fix_sketch: Make the committed `tests/.pre_impl_failures.txt` the only default; accept the QA file exclusively via an explicit `--baseline` argument. Add a `test_ci_gates` assertion that `DEFAULT_BASELINE` is inside `REPO_ROOT`.

findings.title: Three competing failure baselines exist, two of them unversioned and present on exactly one machine
findings.claim: The 'no regressions' decision is made against one of three different artefacts with two different counts — a committed 48-id mirror, an untracked 48-id QA file, and an untracked 46-line comm-gate cache — and the two untracked ones live only in a sibling checkout that `.gitignore` guarantees can never be shared.
findings.evidence: (1) `tests/.pre_impl_failures.txt` — committed, 48 ids. (2) `scripts/regression_gate_diff.py:42` — `C:\Users\SynAckITPC\Documents\AI\smartcompare\.qa-discovery\BASELINE_FAILURES.txt`, verified present on this machine, 48 `FAILED `-prefixed lines, under the `.qa-*/` ignore rule. (3) CLAUDE.md:276 gotcha (g) — "the 46-line prod baseline is cached at `.qa-correctness/main-baseline-failed.txt`"; that directory does not exist in this worktree but `C:\Users\SynAckITPC\Documents\AI\smartcompare\.qa-correctness\main-baseline-failed.txt` does. 48 vs 48 vs 46.
findings.failure_scenario: Three agents run 'the regression gate' on three worktrees and get three answers, and only one of the three inputs is reviewable in a diff. A branch cleared on the 46-line cache can be flagged against the 48-id mirror and vice versa, and neither disagreement leaves a trace — the deciding artefact is gitignored by a rule (`.qa-*/`) added for a good reason (scraped tokens) that also makes the gate unauditable.
findings.fix_sketch: Promote exactly one baseline into the repo (`tests/.pre_impl_failures.txt`), regenerate it, and make the comm-gate harness and `regression_gate_diff` both read it. If QA needs a private capture, have it emit a diff against the committed file rather than replacing it.

findings.title: Four free-tier nodes fail on main but are absent from the committed baseline, so the gate reports a false regression on every branch
findings.claim: A full free-tier run on this pinned main finds 15 failing nodes, but only 11 of them are in the committed 48-id baseline; the other four are red on main itself, so `scripts/regression_gate_diff.py` computing `current - baseline` returns a non-empty `branch-only-NEW` for any branch, whatever it changed.
findings.evidence: Measured full free-tier run (15,598 passed / 19 failed / 52 skipped / 37 xfailed, 4m50s) plus targeted re-runs. Present in the baseline: auth_interceptor x2, backend_cleanup, camera_vision x3, extraction_prompt_bundle_c, personalization_bundle_c x2, referral_e2e, security_regression = 11. ABSENT from `tests/.pre_impl_failures.txt`: `tests/test_page_scraping.py::TestFetchPagePriceJsonLD::test_jsonld_nested_offers_picks_lowest`, `tests/test_page_scraping.py::TestFetchPagePriceOpenGraph::test_og_meta_extraction`, `tests/test_invitee_quiz.py::TestInviteResolutionEdgeCases::test_invalid_token_format_does_not_crash`, `tests/test_supplement_branch_genuine.py::TestCatalogSupplementSourceAttribution::test_cde2_attributes_catalog_supplement_domain_when_flag_on` — all four re-confirmed failing without the socket blocker (`4 failed, 92 passed`). CLAUDE.md:459 nonetheless closes the wave with "test estate 0 failed both flag modes (374/374 formerly-red files)".
findings.failure_scenario: Anyone running the documented gate with the committed baseline (the CI / fresh-clone path, per regression_gate_diff.py:46) sees four 'NEW' failures on a branch that touched nothing, concludes the harness is unreliable, and stops trusting the only regression signal the repo has. The two-worktree `comm` harness hides this by cancelling main against branch — which is precisely why the committed baseline was allowed to drift four nodes behind reality without anyone noticing.
findings.fix_sketch: Re-capture `tests/.pre_impl_failures.txt` from a clean main run (which also drops the two dead ids in tests-ci-06), and add a CI step or a `test_ci_gates` check that re-derives the count so the file cannot silently fall behind main again.

findings.title: Enumerated: 11 free-tier tests make real network calls, of which the docs name 3
findings.claim: Running the whole free tier with sockets and DNS hard-blocked surfaces 8 tests that dial the network beyond the 3 already documented — three SSRF tests that resolve `example.com` through public DNS, three that open a TCP connection to the Supabase host, and (excluded to let the run finish) the two price-cache-bust probes and the rate-limit test.
findings.evidence: Method: a `pytest_configure` plugin replacing `socket.socket.connect`, `connect_ex`, `socket.create_connection` and `socket.getaddrinfo` with raisers for any non-loopback host; full free-tier selection, `--timeout=30`. Delta vs the same selection without the blocker: `tests/test_security_hardening.py::TestSSRFProtection::test_valid_external_url_passes`, `::test_valid_http_url_passes`, `::TestSecurityIntegration::test_ssrf_protection_integrated` (all three via `app/utils/url_validator.py:48` — logged `[SSRF] URL validation error: REAL DNS getaddrinfo -> 'example.com':None`), and `tests/test_conftest_env_safety.py::test_sentinel_hosts_really_do_not_resolve_here` (a deliberate DNS probe). Two more reach `('neutralized.supabase.invalid', 443)` through un-mocked PostgREST calls (`test_invitee_quiz`, `test_supplement_branch_genuine`), i.e. they are only kept off production Supabase by the #48 sentinel host, not by a mock. Already documented: `test_rate_limiting_complete.py` + the two `test_price_cache_bust_probe.py::TestPriceReadBypass` nodes in `scripts/regression_gate_diff.py:55-62`.
findings.failure_scenario: The three SSRF tests pass only because the runner can resolve `example.com`. On a GitHub runner with restricted egress, behind a corporate DNS that NXDOMAIN-hijacks, or on a plane, `validate_url` raises, the assertions flip, and three SECURITY tests go red for environmental reasons — indistinguishable from an actual SSRF-guard regression. The two Supabase ones are the sharper risk: with `LIVE=1` (or if the sentinel is ever changed to a resolvable host) the same un-mocked calls hit production Supabase from the default tier.
findings.fix_sketch: Mock the DNS lookup in the three SSRF tests (`patch('app.utils.url_validator.socket.getaddrinfo')`) so they test the validator's logic rather than the internet; mock the PostgREST client in `test_invitee_quiz` and `test_supplement_branch_genuine`. Then adopt the blocker permanently: ship the plugin as a conftest autouse fixture so any new free-tier test that dials out fails immediately with the host name in the message.

findings.title: An untracked failing test is reporting a real one: the invite-resolution route 500s on any Supabase error
findings.claim: `ReferralService.resolve_invite` promises in its own docstring to return `None` when a lookup fails, but makes both PostgREST calls with no exception handling, so any Supabase error propagates through `referral_routes.py:261` to the global handler as HTTP 500 — which is exactly what `test_invitee_quiz::test_invalid_token_format_does_not_crash` ("garbage token must not crash server") is currently red on.
findings.evidence: `app/services/referral_service.py:388-399` — docstring "Returns ``None`` if either lookup fails", then `rpc_resp = self.client.rpc("resolve_referral_code", {"p_code": ref_code}).execute()` with no try/except; the comparison lookup at `:409` is the same. `app/api/referral_routes.py:260-266` only maps a falsy return to 404. Measured: `GET /api/v1/referrals/invite/abc?ref=QR-XXX` returns 500, with `error_handler.py:141 Unhandled ... create_connection -> ('neutralized.supabase.invalid', 443)`. The node is in neither `tests/.pre_impl_failures.txt` nor the markdown breakdown.
findings.failure_scenario: A Supabase blip, a PostgREST timeout, an RLS policy error or a transient DNS failure turns every invite-link open into a 500 instead of a graceful 404/retry. Invite links are the referral acquisition loop's entire funnel entry: the shared WhatsApp link renders an error screen, the invitee bounces, and the Loop-1 credit is never earned. Sentry sees a spike of unhandled exceptions rather than a handled degradation.
findings.fix_sketch: Wrap both lookups in `try/except Exception: logger.warning(...); return None` so the documented contract holds and the route's existing 404 path handles it. Then add the node to the baseline or fix it — right now it is red and untracked.

findings.title: Two test_page_scraping nodes pin behaviour the repo deliberately reversed, including the explicitly-forbidden smallest-wins rule
findings.claim: `test_jsonld_nested_offers_picks_lowest` asserts the multiplicity policy that CLAUDE.md's M10 A3 ruling explicitly forbids ("query-size wins -> request context -> pend; never smallest-wins"), and `test_og_meta_extraction` pins a confidence constant that has since changed from 0.9 to 0.675 — both red on main, both untracked.
findings.evidence: `tests/test_page_scraping.py:195` — `assert result["amount"] == 425.0`, failing `KeyError: 'amount'` because the runtime now pends: `price_service.py:12840` logs "[PRICE] jsonld multiplicity unresolved on shop.example.com — 2 candidates [425.0, 450.0] (pending, never a silent pick)". `tests/test_page_scraping.py:214` — `assert result["confidence"] == 0.9`, failing `assert 0.675 == 0.9`. CLAUDE.md:336 records the A3 policy as "pinned prose-only (`2ca58f4`) — query-size wins -> request context -> pend; never smallest-wins".
findings.failure_scenario: The first test does not merely fail — it documents the opposite of the shipped policy. A future maintainer following the repo's own rule ("a stale test pinning a removed value" is called out at CLAUDE.md:280 as a thing the dispatcher must catch) could read this assertion as the contract and re-introduce silent smallest-wins picking, which is the exact leak the multiplicity pend exists to prevent. Meanwhile both nodes make the free tier permanently red without appearing on any tracked list.
findings.fix_sketch: Rewrite `test_jsonld_nested_offers_picks_lowest` to assert the pend (no `amount`, a `reason`), rename it accordingly, and update the confidence expectation in `test_og_meta_extraction` to the current constant with a comment naming the commit that changed it.

findings.title: The #48 credential-neutralisation guarantee is verified by two tests that are both inert without a .env — i.e. always inert in CI
findings.claim: The only two tests that assert "no production credential value is live in the test process" cannot fail on a machine with no `.env`: one `pytest.skip`s explicitly and the other's leak comprehension is filtered by a fingerprint map that is all-`None` — so on CI and in every worktree the credential-strip contract has zero effective assertions behind it.
findings.evidence: `tests/test_conftest_env_safety.py:156-165` — `if not env_file.is_file(): pytest.skip("no .env on this machine (CI) -- nothing could leak")`. `:135-141` — `leaked = [name for name in _CONTRACT_UNSET if PRE_SANITIZE_FINGERPRINTS.get(name) and fingerprint(os.getenv(name)) == PRE_SANITIZE_FINGERPRINTS[name]]`; `tests/_env_safety.py:223-227` populates that map from the live environment, so without `.env` every value is `None` and the guard clause short-circuits. Measured in this worktree (no `.env`): `entries: 20 non-None: 0`, and `pytest tests/test_conftest_env_safety.py -rs` gives `24 passed, 3 skipped` with the skip reason "no .env on this machine (CI)". CLAUDE.md gotcha (c) records that worktrees never inherit `.env`, so this is the normal state everywhere except the main checkout.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone deletes or reorders `neutralize_credentials()` / `install_dotenv_guard()` in `tests/conftest.py:28-29` (e.g. while debugging why a test needs a real key). CI stays fully green — the structural half of the file still passes because the sentinels are set by the very code under test — and the only machine that would catch it is the one main checkout that has a `.env`. The regression then ships: local `pytest tests/` starts writing to the production Upstash cache and reporting test exceptions into production Sentry again, which is the exact state #48 was opened to end.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a subprocess-based test that writes a synthetic `.env` into a tmp_path, runs a one-line pytest session with `cwd=tmp_path`, and asserts the synthetic credential is absent from the child's environment — the same shape `test_live_opt_in_restores_the_environment_end_to_end(tmp_path)` at `:561` already uses for the opposite direction. That version runs identically in CI.

findings.title: The pre-commit hook lints the working tree, not the staged content it is gating
findings.claim: Steps 1-3 and 5 of `.githooks/pre-commit` pass PATH NAMES to `py_compile`, `ruff`, `black --check` and `sqlfluff`, so all four read whatever is currently on disk rather than the staged blobs — the hook can pass a commit whose staged content is broken, and fail a commit whose staged content is clean.
findings.evidence: `.githooks/pre-commit:11` collects names with `git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM`, then `:17` `python -m py_compile $PY_FILES`, `:25` `ruff check ... $PY_FILES`, `:42` `python -m black --check $STAGED_ALLOWED`, `:82` `sqlfluff lint --dialect postgres $SQL_FILES`. None uses `git show :<path>` or a `git stash --keep-index` wrapper. By contrast step 4 (`:57`) correctly reads `git diff --cached -U0`, which shows the author knew the distinction.
findings.failure_scenario: `git add app/services/price_service.py` while it has a syntax error, then fix the error in the editor without re-adding, then `git commit` — py_compile and ruff both read the FIXED working-tree file, pass, and the BROKEN staged blob is committed. The mirror case is noisier and more common: `git add -p` a clean hunk while the rest of the file is mid-refactor, and the hook rejects a commit that would have been fine, training everyone to reach for `--no-verify`.
findings.fix_sketch: Materialise the staged content first: `TMP=$(mktemp -d); for f in $PY_FILES; do mkdir -p "$TMP/$(dirname $f)"; git show ":$f" > "$TMP/$f"; done` and run the four checks against `$TMP`. Simpler alternative when no partial staging is expected: wrap the hook body in `git stash push --keep-index --include-untracked` / `git stash pop`.

findings.title: The pre-commit secrets guard matches none of the credential shapes this repo actually holds
findings.claim: The staged-diff credential regex covers `sk-…`, `AKIA…`, `xox[baprs]-…` and PEM private keys, which between them match exactly one of the repo's eight documented secrets — Supabase's JWT service key, the Upstash token, the Serper/Firecrawl/Scrape.do/Zyte/Bright Data keys and `ADMIN_API_KEY` all pass the guard unchallenged.
findings.evidence: `.githooks/pre-commit:57-60` — `grep -qE '(\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|xox[baprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}|-----BEGIN (RSA |EC |OPENSSH )?PRIVATE KEY-----)'`. CLAUDE.md:323 lists the required secrets as `OPENAI_API_KEY, SERPER_API_KEY, SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY, UPSTASH_REDIS_URL, UPSTASH_REDIS_TOKEN, ADMIN_API_KEY`; `tests/_env_safety.py:110-133` adds `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`, `SCRAPEDO_API_TOKEN`, `BRIGHTDATA_API_KEY`, `ZYTE_API_KEY`, `NASSER_GUEST_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_DSN`. Only `OPENAI_API_KEY` has the `sk-` shape. `.gitignore:60-63` documents a real prior near-miss ("recon dumps can contain live tokens — e.g. .qa-bh-sourcing/_f3_nasser_main.js carries a scraped guest token"), i.e. the exact class this guard is supposed to stop.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent pastes a Supabase service-role JWT (`eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...`) into a runbook, a fixture `SOURCES.json`, or a debugging snippet and stages it. The guard sees no `sk-`/`AKIA`/`xox`/PEM match and the commit succeeds; a service-role key — which bypasses every RLS policy in `migrations/` — lands in git history and, if the repo is ever pushed public or a fork is shared, is permanently exposed.
findings.fix_sketch: Add the missing shapes to the same alternation: `eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}` (JWT), `\bfc-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}` (Firecrawl), `\bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}` (GitHub), `\bAIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35}` (Google), and a generic `\b[A-Za-z0-9_-]{32,}\b` guarded to lines that also contain `KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|DSN=`. Keep the `\b` anchoring lesson recorded in the existing comment at `:50-56`.

findings.title: The coverage floor measures app/ only — scripts/ (13,418 lines of cron, eval and gate code) has no floor at all
findings.claim: `--cov=app` scopes the only enforced coverage floor to `app/`, leaving `scripts/` — 38 modules and 13,418 lines including the price-cache warmer, the nightly eval cron, the sitemap indexer, the seeding scripts and the regression gate itself — with zero measured coverage and no floor.
findings.evidence: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:93-95` = `--cov=app --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=83`; no `--cov=scripts` anywhere in either workflow. `find scripts -name '*.py' | wc -l` = 38, total 13,418 lines. `tests/` does exercise some of it (`test_eval_runner.py`, `test_regression_gate_diff.py`, `test_cron_reengagement.py`, `test_cron_eval_nightly.py`, `test_seed_zyte_guard.py`), so the coverage is nonzero but unmeasured. CLAUDE.md:326 documents `scripts/cron_warm_price_cache.py:118-131` as budget-critical operational logic.
findings.failure_scenario: A refactor deletes or short-circuits a branch in `scripts/cron_warm_price_cache.py` (the genuine-price lever that spends the finite Serper budget) or in `scripts/regression_gate_diff.py` (the gate). Coverage for `app/` is unchanged, `--cov-fail-under=83` passes, and the collapse is invisible until an off-clock cron either burns budget or silently stops warming. The gate script losing coverage is the sharpest case: the tool that decides "no new regressions" is itself outside the only regression signal CI enforces.
findings.fix_sketch: Change to `--cov=app --cov=scripts` and set the floor from the first measured combined run (the same ratchet procedure d48bc19 used for 60->83). If the combined number is too low to floor immediately, add `--cov=scripts` with `--cov-report=term-missing` only and ratchet later.

findings.title: The documented Nasser kill switch only responds to the literal string 'false', and no test exercises the env path at all
findings.claim: `ENABLE_NASSER_ADAPTER` (and `ENABLE_PAGE_SCRAPE`, `ENABLE_FIRECRAWL`, `ENABLE_SCRAPEDO`) parse as `os.environ.get(NAME, "true").lower() != "false"`, so `0`, `off`, `no` and `disabled` all leave the feature ON; every test in the estate patches the resulting module boolean instead of the env var, so the parse itself is never executed by a test.
findings.evidence: `app/services/price_service.py:14840` `ENABLE_NASSER_ADAPTER = os.environ.get("ENABLE_NASSER_ADAPTER", "true").lower() != "false"` under a comment at `:14837` reading "MED-2 kill switch — flip ENABLE_NASSER_ADAPTER=false in Railway to disable the adapter entirely (e.g. token permanently dead ...)". Same shape at `price_service.py:41`, `firecrawl_service.py:134`, `scrapedo_service.py:104`. AST scan of all 535 test files: zero `monkeypatch.setenv`/`delenv`/`os.environ[...]` sites for any of these four names; `tests/test_nasser_adapter.py:217,263,276,330` uses `monkeypatch.setattr(ps, "ENABLE_NASSER_ADAPTER", True/False)`, i.e. the post-parse boolean.
findings.failure_scenario: The Nasser guest token gets rotated and the adapter starts hammering a dead credential. An operator follows the comment's intent and sets `ENABLE_NASSER_ADAPTER=0` (or `off`) in Railway. `"0" != "false"` is True, so the adapter stays fully enabled and keeps firing — and no test anywhere would have caught the difference, because the entire test estate reaches past the parse. The same trap disables nothing for `ENABLE_PAGE_SCRAPE`, the master curl_cffi switch.
findings.fix_sketch: Route all four through one shared truthy helper (the `("true","1","yes","on")` set already used by `sitemap_discovery_service.py:919`) with an inverted default, and add one parametrised test per flag that drives the ENV var through `monkeypatch.setenv` over `{'false','0','off','no','FALSE'}` and asserts the resulting behaviour, not the module global.

findings.title: ENABLE_SITEMAP_INDEX is the one activation-runbook flag no test ever sets; its env reader is patched out everywhere
findings.claim: `_sitemap_index_cron_enabled()` is the env→bool reader that decides whether a Tier-3 negative cache entry lives 24h or 30d, and every test that reaches it replaces it with `patch.object(sds, "_sitemap_index_cron_enabled", return_value=...)`; across all 535 test files no test ever sets `ENABLE_SITEMAP_INDEX`, so the reader's own truthy set is unexecuted.
findings.evidence: `app/services/sitemap_discovery_service.py:915-922` returns `os.getenv("ENABLE_SITEMAP_INDEX", "").strip().lower() in ("true","1","yes","on")`; `:939-944` short-circuits `sitemap_discovery_is_cold()` on it, and `app/services/structured_comparison_service.py:6963` feeds that into `transient_discovery=`. `grep -rn ENABLE_SITEMAP_INDEX tests/` returns two hits, both inside comments (`test_robots_unreadable_ruling.py:32`, `test_transient_negcache.py:53`). All six behavioural tests in `tests/test_transient_negcache.py:45-78` patch the function out. AST flag-matrix over the whole tree: ENABLE_SITEMAP_INDEX has 0 ON and 0 OFF env toggles — the only flag in CLAUDE.md:338's activation runbook with neither.
findings.failure_scenario: Step (3) of the activation runbook flips `ENABLE_SITEMAP_INDEX=true`. If the reader is wrong — a typo in the truthy tuple, a `.strip()` regression, or Railway supplying `True` with a capital T (already covered) versus `enabled` (not) — `sitemap_discovery_is_cold()` silently keeps returning False and every structural-gap estimate stays on the 30d path, so the whole sitemap channel activation is a no-op that looks successful. The inverse is worse: if it turns on when it should not, negative-cache TTLs drop 30d->24h across every sitemap category and the full scrape cascade re-runs ~30x more often against the finite Serper/Firecrawl budget. Nothing in 15,728 test nodes distinguishes those outcomes.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a parametrised test in `tests/test_transient_negcache.py` that drives `monkeypatch.setenv("ENABLE_SITEMAP_INDEX", v)` over `{'true','True','1','yes','on','','false','0','off','TRUE '}` and asserts `sds._sitemap_index_cron_enabled()` directly — the one seam the existing six tests all bypass.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md and the wave-1 handoff both document a coverage floor of 60; ci.yml has been 83 since d48bc19
findings.claim: Two documents instruct the next maintainer to raise `--cov-fail-under` from a "deliberately 60" placeholder, but the ratchet already happened: `ci.yml:95` reads `--cov-fail-under=83`, and the ratchet commit is in this tree's history.
findings.evidence: `CLAUDE.md:403` — "`--cov-fail-under` is deliberately 60 vs a measured 78 — raise it to the number CI now reports." `docs/investigations/2026-08-25-audit-wave1-handoff.md:41` — "`--cov-fail-under` is deliberately 60 against a locally-measured 78. Raise it to the number CI now reports, rounded down." `.github/workflows/ci.yml:95` — `--cov-fail-under=83`. `git log --oneline -- .github/workflows/ci.yml` shows `d48bc19 ci: ratchet the coverage floor from 60 to the measured 83 (#91)`.
findings.failure_scenario: A session picks up the documented task "raise the coverage floor", edits ci.yml expecting to find 60, finds 83, and burns a cycle re-deriving what already shipped — or, worse, trusts the doc, concludes CI has no real floor, and skips coverage entirely when reviewing a change that drops it from 84% to 83.1%, one tenth of a point above a floor everyone believes is 60.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace both sentences with "`--cov-fail-under` is 83, ratcheted in #91 from the first CI measurement of 84.85%; re-ratchet after the #89 failures are fixed."

findings.title: ci.yml's coverage comment block contradicts itself: it records the 83 ratchet and then argues at length for 60
findings.claim: The comment above the coverage step states the floor was raised to 83 (lines 63-67) and is immediately followed by 17 lines of superseded reasoning that concludes "So: 60 — about 18 points of margin below the measurement" and instructs the reader to "RATCHET IT UP ... after the first green run on main" — a step that already happened.
findings.evidence: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:63-67` ("RATCHETED 2026-08-25: the first green CI run on main measured 84.85% ... so the placeholder 60 was raised to 83") vs `:69-85` ("HOW THE FLOOR WAS SET, and why it sits deliberately below the measurement ... So: 60 ... RATCHET IT UP to the observed CI percentage (rounded down) after the first green run on main"). Both blocks describe the same `--cov-fail-under` at `:95`.
findings.failure_scenario: The next person to touch the coverage gate reads a 25-line comment that names two different floors and gives an already-completed instruction. The likely resolutions are both wrong: lower it back to 60 (removing a real gate) or ratchet it again from a number the stale half of the comment implies is the baseline.
findings.fix_sketch: Delete lines 69-85; keep 63-67 and append the one fact worth preserving from the deleted block — that the CI environment has no `.env` and so runs ~150 more error paths than a local measurement.

findings.title: Two Bundle-C RED-by-design stubs redden CI while the identical 35-stub class next to them is xfail-contained
findings.claim: `test_applied_shifts_list_is_default_empty_when_no_priorities` and `test_full_response_payload_audit_no_magnitude_keys` are explicit `pytest.fail("RED: ... wiring pending")` stubs for an unimplemented `build_comparison_response(personalization=...)` kwarg — exactly the class that issue #49 contained for `tests/test_value_math.py` — but they carry no xfail and so contribute 2 of the ~13 failures keeping `backend-tests` red.
findings.evidence: `tests/test_personalization_bundle_c.py:179-188` catches `TypeError` from the missing kwarg and calls `pytest.fail("RED: build_comparison_response personalization wiring pending")`; `:132-147` does the same with "A.x wiring pending". Measured: `TypeError: build_comparison_response() got an unexpected keyword argument 'personalization'`. Compare `tests/test_value_math.py:63` — `pytestmark = pytest.mark.xfail(reason="RED-by-design: Bundle C v1.1 ... not implemented yet", strict=False)` — and `tests/test_ci_gates.py:77-116`, which exists specifically to keep that containment honest.
findings.failure_scenario: Two of the failures blocking `backend-tests` from becoming a required status check are not defects at all — they are TDD placeholders for a feature that was never scheduled. Anyone working issue #89 ("the last 15 failures") spends time diagnosing them, discovers there is nothing to fix without shipping Bundle C personalization, and the job stays red for a reason no code change can address.
findings.fix_sketch: Give the two tests the same treatment as value_math: a module-scoped `pytest.mark.xfail(reason=..., strict=False)` plus an expiry guard in `test_ci_gates.py` that goes red when `build_comparison_response` gains the `personalization` parameter. That drops the effective baseline from 13 to 11 and makes the remaining set actionable.

findings.title: test_backend_cleanup pins a source-text property that has legitimately reverted — pure rot
findings.claim: `TestDeadFunctionsRemoved::test_unused_imports_cleaned` asserts `"import os" not in inspect.getsource(app.services.openai_service)`; `openai_service.py` imports `os` again for legitimate reasons, so the test encodes a one-time cleanup as a permanent invariant and can only ever be red.
findings.evidence: `tests/test_backend_cleanup.py:163` — `assert "import os" not in source, "Unused 'os' import should be cleaned up"`, reached via `inspect.getsource(mod)` at `:159-161`. Measured failure message: `'import os' is contained here: ... import os / from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional`. `app/services/openai_service.py` uses `os.getenv` for the model-config and base-URL resolution added by #58.
findings.failure_scenario: The assertion is a substring search over a module's own source text: it also matches `import ossl`, a docstring mentioning "import os", or a comment. It cannot be made to pass without deleting a genuinely-used import, so it will sit in the baseline forever, and it teaches by example that a source-text grep is an acceptable regression test — a pattern already replicated in `test_security_regression.py`'s console.log scanner (see tests-ci-19).
findings.fix_sketch: Delete the assertion (the dead functions it was paired with are gone; their absence is what `test_dead_functions_removed` already checks) and remove the node from `tests/.pre_impl_failures.txt`. If import hygiene is wanted, ruff's F401 already covers it repo-wide.

findings.title: test_referral_e2e fails on stale fixture data that migration 021's regex has rejected since it landed
findings.claim: `test_e2e_share_creates_invite_and_grants_loop1_credit` posts `device_fingerprint_hash="smoke-referrer-device-hash"`, which cannot match the `^[a-f0-9]{64}$` pattern migration 021 introduced, so the route returns 422 and the test's mocked ReferralService is never reached — the failure is fixture rot, not a referral defect.
findings.evidence: Measured failure at `tests/test_referral_e2e.py:133`: `assert 422 == 201` with body `"Validation error: body -> device_fingerprint_hash: String should match pattern '^[a-f0-9]{64}$'"`. CLAUDE.md:83 documents migration **021** as adding `users.device_fingerprint_hash` with a partial index that "matches `^[a-f0-9]{64}$`". `tests/PRE_IMPL_FAILURE_BASELINE.md:55` records this node only as "Referral e2e; pre-existing".
findings.failure_scenario: The whole point of the e2e smoke chain is to prove share -> invite -> Loop-1 credit end to end. Because the request is rejected at validation, the chain has verified nothing since migration 021 shipped, while sitting in the baseline as an accepted failure — so a real break in `create_invite`, the share-link builder or the referral-code stamp would be invisible. It is also the cheapest of the 13 to fix: one literal.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace the literal with a valid digest, e.g. `hashlib.sha256(b"smoke-referrer-device").hexdigest()`, and remove the node from the baseline. Add the same helper to the other referral fixtures so the class cannot recur.

findings.title: A DO-NOT-SKIP security regression test is red on one real leak and one false positive from a line-based scanner
findings.claim: `test_no_bare_console_log_in_auth` reports two violations: line 480 is a genuine un-`__DEV__`-guarded `console.log` that prints the first 24 characters of a Google ID token, and line 599 is a false positive caused by the scanner matching single lines, unable to see that the call sits inside an `if (__DEV__)` block.
findings.evidence: `SmartCompareApp/src/services/authService.ts:479-480` — `const diagHead = \`len=${idToken.length} parts=${parts.length} head=${idToken.substring(0, 24)}\`; console.log('[GOOGLE-DIAG]', diagHead);` with no `__DEV__` guard. `:597-605` — `if (__DEV__) { const parts = ...; console.log(` — a multi-line call whose first line contains neither `__DEV__` nor a closing paren. The detector at `tests/test_security_regression.py:507-510` tests `stripped.startswith("console.") and "__DEV__" not in line`, i.e. per-line with no block awareness. CLAUDE.md:227 marks this file's ~98 tests "DO NOT delete or skip".
findings.failure_scenario: Two independent costs. (1) A production RN build logs `head=<first 24 chars of the Google id_token>` to the device log on every Google sign-in, where any log-collection SDK or a connected debugger can read it. (2) Because the same test also reports a false positive, the node was baselined wholesale as "intentional Google diagnostic instrumentation" — so the file is now unmonitored: a genuinely new bare `console.log` leaking a refresh token would add a third line to a message nobody reads, inside a failure everyone has agreed to ignore.
findings.fix_sketch: Wrap line 480 in `if (__DEV__)` (or delete it — the Sentry breadcrumb on the next line already captures the same data). Then make the detector block-aware: track whether the current line is inside an `if (__DEV__) {` brace depth, so the line-599 false positive disappears and the test can leave the baseline.

findings.title: response_builder does not strip the internal flags its own regression test says it must
findings.claim: `test_response_builder_strips_inference_source` asserts a belt-and-braces invariant — internal keys never reach the serialised response — that is simply not implemented: `_internal` is filtered only inside the SPEC dict, and a product-level `_internal` is echoed verbatim.
findings.evidence: `app/services/response_builder.py:313-318` — `_SPEC_INTERNAL_FIELDS = {"_field_confidence", "_internal", "_extraction_metadata"}` with the comment "Spec fields with internal-only / metadata semantics — never emit as comparable rows on Screen 4", i.e. scoped to spec rows. Reproduced directly: calling `build_comparison_response(products=[{'name':'iPhone','specs':{...},'price':{...},'_internal':{'processor_inference_source':'model_knowledge'}}, ...])` returns a product dict containing `"_internal": {"processor_inference_source": "model_knowledge"}`. `grep -rn '_internal' app/ --include=*.py` outside the score-scrub helpers returns exactly one hit — that constant — so nothing produces the key today.
findings.failure_scenario: The leak is latent only because no current code path attaches `_internal` to a product. The moment any extraction change stamps provenance there (which is precisely what the key is named for), it ships to every API client with no code change to the response builder — and the test that exists to catch that has already been reclassified as an accepted baseline failure, so it will not fire.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a top-level strip in `build_comparison_response`: pop any key in `_SPEC_INTERNAL_FIELDS` (or any leading-underscore key) from each product dict before serialisation, mirroring the spec-level filter. The test then passes and leaves the baseline.

findings.title: One un-mocked free-tier test hangs past the pytest timeout and, under the Windows thread method, kills the whole run
findings.claim: `TestRateLimitCoverage::test_prices_endpoint_rate_limited` drives the real price pipeline in-process through `TestClient`, so it blocks on live network; on Windows pytest-timeout's thread method dumps stacks and terminates the interpreter, aborting every test after it rather than failing one node.
findings.evidence: `tests/test_rate_limiting_complete.py:34` — `resp = client.get("/api/v1/text/prices/test-product")` against `TestClient(app)`. Measured: a full free-tier run with real sockets blocked and `--timeout=45` produced a `+++ Timeout +++` stack dump whose deepest frames are `testclient.py:378 portal.call(self.app, ...) -> concurrent/futures/_base.py:451 self._condition.wait(timeout) -> threading.py:355 waiter.acquire()`, and the process ended at `[ 74%]` — the remaining ~4,100 nodes never ran. `python -c "import locale; locale.getpreferredencoding(False)"` = cp1252, i.e. the documented Windows dev platform where pytest-timeout defaults to the thread method (SIGALRM is unavailable).
findings.failure_scenario: A developer runs the documented free-unit command on Windows. Somewhere around 74% the interpreter is killed with a wall of stack text and no summary line, so the run reports nothing about the 4,100 nodes after it. The natural reading is 'the suite is broken'; the actual cause is one test making a real request. CLAUDE.md:440 records the hang but not that it aborts the run, which is why the advice there is the vague 'run targeted file sets'.
findings.fix_sketch: Mark the node `@pytest.mark.live_unit` so the conftest hook skips it without `LIVE=1` (it is already in `NETWORK_FLAKY_EXCLUDE`, so nothing else depends on it running), or mock `_get_price` in the fixture so the rate-limit assertion tests the limiter rather than the pipeline. Either removes the abort and makes the free tier finishable on Windows.

findings.title: 35 encoding-less read_text() calls in tests, 11 of whose targets already hold non-ASCII, on a cp1252 machine
findings.claim: The static source-scanning tests read their targets with `Path(...).read_text()` and no `encoding=`, in direct violation of the repo's own Windows rule; 11 of the 12 files they read already contain UTF-8 multi-byte sequences that are being silently mis-decoded as cp1252.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'read_text()' tests/ | wc -l` = 35 (e.g. `test_security_regression.py:502,67,143,199,213,281`). Measured on this machine: `locale.getpreferredencoding(False)` = `cp1252`, `PYTHONUTF8` unset, `sys.flags.utf8_mode` = 0; of the 12 distinct paths read this way, 11 contain non-ASCII bytes (`app/api/admin_routes.py` 60 bytes, `SmartCompareApp/src/services/authService.ts` 46, `app/services/auth_service.py` 21, `app/main.py` 9, ...). CLAUDE.md:373 states the rule: "always pass `encoding='utf-8'` to `subprocess.run`/`open`/`read_text` — `text=True` alone decodes cp1252 and manufactures mojibake from clean UTF-8".
findings.failure_scenario: cp1252 leaves five byte values undefined (0x81, 0x8D, 0x8F, 0x90, 0x9D) and none appear in these files yet, which is the only reason the tests pass. Arabic UTF-8 hits 0x81 directly: `'\u0641'` (ARABIC LETTER FEH, one of the most common letters) encodes as `b'\xd9\x81'` and `b'\xd9\x81'.decode('cp1252')` raises `UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x81`. This is a Bahrain product with an Arabic UI: the first Arabic string added to `authService.ts` or `api.ts` — both read encoding-less — turns the ~98-test `test_security_regression.py` estate into a collection-time error on every Windows dev machine, exactly the file CLAUDE.md marks DO NOT delete or skip.
findings.fix_sketch: Sweep `read_text()` -> `read_text(encoding="utf-8")` across tests/ (35 sites) and add the same to the 18 encoding-less `open()` calls. Then add a ruff/`test_ci_gates` guard: assert no `read_text()` or `open(` in tests/ lacks an explicit encoding.

findings.title: The prod-host marker ratchet only inspects tests that already carry live_unit, so an unmarked prod-writing test is not caught
findings.claim: `test_every_production_host_live_test_is_marked_live_prod` skips any node without `live_unit` in its marker set, so a test aimed at the production deployment that carries NO marker at all passes the ratchet and would then run on every PR — the one place the production write actually matters most.
findings.evidence: `tests/test_ci_gates.py:708` — `if "live_unit" in marks and "live_prod" not in marks and touches_prod(node): offenders.append(...)`. The workflow header it protects (`.github/workflows/live-suite.yml:37-46`) correctly states the risk is that "any test that makes an HTTP call to the production deployment MAKES PRODUCTION WRITE, whatever query string it sends". I enumerated the 16 test files mentioning `web-production-58776`: five carry no live marker (`test_cron_eval_nightly.py`, `test_scoring_v2_all_nine_categories.py`, `test_security_regression.py`, `test_sentry_service.py`, `test_share_routes.py`), and all five use the host only as an assertion literal or a mocked value — so the gap is currently unexploited.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone adds a convenience smoke test that POSTs to `https://web-production-58776.up.railway.app/api/v1/text/compare` and forgets every marker. `test_every_production_host_live_test_is_marked_live_prod` passes (no `live_unit`), the free-tier marker expression does not deselect it (no marker to deselect on), and the PR gate now spends production vendor budget and writes to the production price cache and L2 price rows on every push to every branch.
findings.fix_sketch: Invert the condition: flag any test node whose source touches PROD_HOST unless it carries `live_prod` (or is provably assertion-only). Simplest robust form — require that any node touching the host carries at least one of `live_unit`/`live_prod`/`integration`/`bench`.

findings.title: The black 'ratchet' has not gained a single file since it was created and is 62% empty __init__.py
findings.claim: The blocking black gate covers 16 paths of which 10 are zero-content `__init__.py` files, i.e. 6 real files out of 678 under app/tests/scripts (0.9%), and `git log` shows the allowlist has never been modified since the commit that introduced it — so the 'visibly shrinks as files graduate' mechanism the workflow comment promises has never operated.
findings.evidence: `.github/black-clean-paths.txt` non-comment entries: 10 `__init__.py` (app, app/api, app/core, app/models, app/services, app/utils, scripts, tests, tests/fixtures/lane1, tests/perf) plus `app/services/prompt_personalities.py`, `tests/test_ci_gates.py`, `tests/test_fan_out_budget_env.py`, `tests/test_parallel_race_escalation.py`, `tests/test_price_consolidation.py`, `tests/test_registry_ounass_bh_l12.py`. `git log --oneline -- .github/black-clean-paths.txt` = one commit, `a982207`. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:143-146` claims the report-only step "stays here so the number is measured on every run and visibly shrinks as files graduate onto the allowlist above."
findings.failure_scenario: Nine implementation waves (M0-M12) added code without a single file joining the allowlist, so the blocking format gate applies to essentially nothing while consuming a job step, a pinned dependency (`black==26.5.1`, maintained in three places per the TODO at ci.yml:118) and a hook step. The measurable cost is the maintenance of a gate with a ~1% blast radius plus the false confidence that formatting is enforced.
findings.fix_sketch: Either retire the allowlist and accept one repo-wide reformat commit (`black app/ tests/ scripts/`, then flip the repo-wide step to blocking), or make graduation automatic: regenerate the allowlist in CI from `black --check` output and fail only when a previously-clean file regresses.

findings.title: The scheduled live suite installs pytest unpinned and skips the dev lock, so a tooling break reports as scraper drift
findings.claim: The weekly live-adapter job installs `pytest pytest-asyncio pytest-timeout` with no version constraints instead of `requirements-dev.txt`, so it runs on whatever versions PyPI serves that Monday — a different set from the PR gate's pinned `pytest==9.1.1` / `pytest-asyncio==1.4.0` / `pytest-timeout==2.4.0` — and its failure reporter attributes any red run to storefront drift.
findings.evidence: `.github/workflows/live-suite.yml:137-140` — `pip install -r requirements.txt` then `pip install pytest pytest-asyncio pytest-timeout`; `requirements-dev.txt` pins those three exactly and is not installed. The failure handler at `:190-218` opens an issue titled "Live adapter suite failed — likely scraper drift" whose body asserts "a failure usually means a storefront changed its markup and an adapter needs fixing — not that a test is wrong."
findings.failure_scenario: pytest-asyncio ships a breaking default-mode change (it has, twice) on a Sunday. Monday 04:00 UTC the live suite errors at collection, the reporter files 'likely scraper drift', and whoever triages it spends the session re-sampling live storefronts and multi-sampling adapters per the issue's own instructions — for a dependency bump. The run also burns Serper/Firecrawl/Zyte credits before failing.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace the second install with `pip install -r requirements-dev.txt` (it already carries all three pins plus pillow), and add a step-1 collection smoke (`pytest --collect-only -q -m 'live_unit and not live_prod'`) so a tooling break fails before any vendor call is made.

findings.title: frontend-typecheck is continue-on-error, so the TS error count is unbounded and undetected
findings.claim: The only frontend job in CI runs `npx tsc --noEmit` with `continue-on-error: true` and a comment claiming '7 pre-existing TS errors'; nothing pins that number, so the job cannot fail and the error count can grow without limit.
findings.evidence: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:203-205` — `run: cd SmartCompareApp && npx tsc --noEmit` / `continue-on-error: true  # 7 pre-existing TS errors`. There is no baseline file, no `|| test $(count) -le 7` guard, and no test in `tests/test_ci_gates.py` asserting anything about this job (its `test_ci_keeps_existing_backend_and_frontend_jobs` at `:186` only checks the job exists).
findings.failure_scenario: Combined with tests-ci-02 (no Jest job), the React Native app has zero enforced automated checks: type errors accumulate silently behind a green check mark, and the '7' in the comment becomes folklore. A `tsc` error introduced with a screen refactor reaches TestFlight because CI reported success.
findings.fix_sketch: Capture the current count into `.github/ts-error-baseline.txt`, replace `continue-on-error` with a ratchet step (`npx tsc --noEmit | grep -c 'error TS' | ...` fail if greater than baseline), and drive the baseline to zero the way `backend-lint` drove the ruff tier.

findings.title: A binary coverage database and six response dumps are tracked in git at the repo root
findings.claim: `.coverage` (a 53KB machine-local SQLite coverage database) plus six root-level JSON response dumps totalling ~129KB are tracked, and `.gitignore` lists none of them despite ignoring the neighbouring `response_*.json` and `/test_*.py` classes.
findings.evidence: `git ls-files` returns `.coverage`, `full_response.json`, `session23_test_response.json`, `tmp_result.json`, `tmp_result2.json`, `UsersSynAckITPCDocumentsAIsmartcomparetmp_luxury_test.json`, `UsersSynAckITPCDocumentsAIsmartcomparetmp_result.json`. `.gitignore` has a '# Debug/test artifacts (root only)' section covering `response_*.json` and `/test_*.py` but not these. Two filenames are mangled absolute Windows paths (`UsersSynAckITPCDocumentsAIsmartcompare...`), i.e. an output redirect that lost its separators.
findings.failure_scenario: `.coverage` is a coverage.py SQLite file keyed to absolute paths from one machine; whenever anyone runs coverage locally it is rewritten, so it shows up dirty in `git status` on every clone, gets committed by an agent doing `git add -A`, and produces meaningless binary diffs. The dumps are unreviewable prod-response captures that nothing reads — and they are exactly the class `.gitignore:60-63` warns can carry live tokens.
findings.fix_sketch: `git rm --cached .coverage full_response.json session23_test_response.json tmp_result*.json UsersSynAck*.json` and extend the root-only ignore block with `/.coverage`, `/tmp_*.json`, `/full_response.json`, `/session23_*.json`. Check the removed dumps for credentials before concluding history is clean.

findings.title: The value_math xfail reason points at a CLAUDE.md line number that now names a different paragraph
findings.claim: The module-level xfail reason directs the reader to `CLAUDE.md:399` for the RED-by-design rationale; that line is now inside the 'NOTHING MERGED IS ACTIVE UNTIL ENV VARS ARE SET' block, and the value-math bullet has moved to line 372.
findings.evidence: `tests/test_value_math.py:63-68` — `reason=("RED-by-design: Bundle C v1.1 value-math (A.6.x) is not implemented yet — see CLAUDE.md:399 and tests/PRE_IMPL_FAILURE_BASELINE.md")`. `sed -n '399p' CLAUDE.md` = "**NOTHING MERGED IS ACTIVE UNTIL ENV VARS ARE SET — all three ship deliberately inert:**". `grep -n 'Known RED-by-design' CLAUDE.md` = 372. The reason string is printed by `-rxX` on every CI run (ci.yml:92), so 35 xfail lines per run carry the wrong pointer.
findings.failure_scenario: CLAUDE.md is 85KB and edited most sessions, so a pinned line number in a test's failure output is guaranteed to drift. Someone reading the CI xfail summary follows the pointer, lands on an unrelated paragraph about Railway env vars, and concludes the xfail is undocumented — the precise confusion the reason string exists to prevent.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace `CLAUDE.md:399` with a stable anchor — the section name ("CLAUDE.md § Tests, 'Known RED-by-design'") or the issue number (#49), both of which survive edits.

findings.title: Stale xfail narration in test_cascade_order_regression_qa: the file describes an xfail estate it no longer has
findings.claim: The file's docstrings still say its assertions 'are xfail-strict now and flip green TOGETHER when the consolidated branch lands', but the marks were removed and the file is 17 passed / 0 xfailed.
findings.evidence: `tests/test_cascade_order_regression_qa.py:313` — "are xfail-strict now and flip green TOGETHER when the consolidated branch lands"; `:357-359` — "RED-first (xfail strict) ... this is xfail NOW and becomes xpass (loud, strict) when the skip lands." `grep -n 'pytest.mark.xfail' ` on the file returns nothing. Measured: `pytest tests/test_cascade_order_regression_qa.py -q -rxX` = `17 passed`. `LANE_STATE.md:33` still records the old state as "11 passed, 5 xfailed".
findings.failure_scenario: The whole-repo xfail estate is exactly three marks (35 nodes in test_value_math.py plus one strict mark each in test_kpi_truth_modernization.py:73 and test_correctness_coverage_sweep_fixes.py:229), but grepping for 'xfail' returns 40+ hits, most of them narration like this. Anyone auditing what is deliberately red — the task this file's prose is written for — has to run pytest to find out, and LANE_STATE.md hands them a number that is two states old.
findings.fix_sketch: Rewrite the three comment blocks in the past tense ('was xfail-strict until <commit>; now green') and correct LANE_STATE.md:33. Cheap, and it makes `grep xfail tests/` a usable inventory again.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md documents a ~100-file test estate that is actually 535 files and 15,839 nodes
findings.claim: The Tests section states "~100 test files (`test_<feature>.py`, one per service)", understating the estate by more than 5x and mis-describing its organising principle.
findings.evidence: `CLAUDE.md:368`. Measured: `ls tests/*.py | wc -l` = 534 plus `tests/perf/test_latency_bench.py`; `pytest --collect-only` reports `15728/15839 tests collected` for the free-tier selection and 8,424 top-level test functions. The 'one per service' rule no longer holds either — the largest cluster is per-wave/per-finding files (`test_m6_c1_...`, `test_correctness_coverage_sweep_fixes.py`, `test_kpi_truth_modernization.py`).
findings.failure_scenario: Planning decisions keyed off this number are wrong by 5x: 'run the free unit tests' reads as a ~2-minute action rather than a multi-thousand-node run, and the gate-batch rule at CLAUDE.md:532 ('build the gate's file set by grepping the test tree for imports of every changed module') is far more expensive than the doc implies. It also hides the real growth: the estate is now large enough that collection alone takes 21s.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace with the measured figures and the actual naming convention, and note the two shapes that exist (per-service files and per-wave/per-finding files).
